item.title: PAX Good Behavior Game Program
item.description:
The PAX Good Behavior Game is a research-based classroom strategy that promotes positive student choices and collaboration. The program supports a calmer, more focused learning environment by encouraging kindness, teamwork, and respectful behavior among students.

Students have access to monthly calendars with daily PAX activities including acts of kindness, skill-building exercises, and family engagement opportunities throughout August and September 2026.

item.title: School Bus Safety Code of Conduct
item.description:
Talawanda prioritizes bus safety with a progressive discipline system for misconduct. Violations result in escalating consequences: 1st offense - warning and conference; 2nd - parent call and documentation; 3rd - 3-day suspension; 4th - 5-day bus suspension with parent conference; 5th - removal from bus for semester or minimum 10 days. Key safety rules: stay seated facing forward, keep aisle clear, listen to driver, don't distract driver, wait for driver's signal before crossing, and always cross in front of bus while looking both ways.

item.description:

item.title: PBIS Cafeteria Expectations Program
item.description:
Talawanda High School continues its Positive Behavioral Interventions and Supports (PBIS) program with exciting student recognition opportunities. Students can earn Bogan Brave Tickets from staff for following expectations, with weekly Friday prize drawings by Dr. Cannon. Monthly Student of the Month awards recognize students demonstrating specific character traits, earning certificates, photos, and Good News Calls home.

Cafeteria expectations include: Be Kind (use appropriate language, say please/thank you, welcome everyone, help peers, listen to tablemates), Be Safe (enter/exit quietly with walking feet, stay seated, keep hands/feet to self, share food only from share table), and Be Responsible (use 3-inch voice, raise hand for help, follow adult directions, use tools appropriately, keep table and floor clean).

item.title: School Nurse Welcome and Health Requirements
item.description:
The school nurse welcomes families back and reminds Kindergarten families to submit required physical and immunization records. Students needing medication during school must complete a School Medication Permit form (available at https://www.talawanda.org/media/user/resources/Form_SchoolMedicalPermit.pdf), which must be filled out by a healthcare provider for prescribed medications. For questions or concerns, contact the nurse at Bears@talawanda.org (preferred) or by phone, though response times may vary as student care is the top priority.

item.title: Student Attendance Policy and Chronic Absenteeism
item.description:
Attendance is essential for student success. Ohio defines chronic absenteeism as missing 10% or more of the school year (excused or unexcused), calculated by hours missed—including tardies and early dismissals. Families will receive monthly letters if their student reaches 10% absence threshold. The school encourages families to take planned trips but asks them to be mindful of other absences, and offers help for any attendance concerns.
